body: Activation steering is a powerful training-free paradigm for controlling large language models at inference time. However, standard approaches estimate a per-layer steering direction from contrastive data and apply it on the layer's entire representation space, which may couple the intervention to off-target properties present in the contrastive data and degrade unrelated capabilities. To mitigate this issue, we introduce LocUS (Localized Unembedding Steering), a method which grounds activation steering to the model's own output vocabulary subspace. By identifying a property-specific linear subspace within the unembedding matrix, LocUS enforces a geometric constraint that restricts the steering transformation to a specific subspace and at the same time localizes its application to a sparse subset of attention heads. Extensive evaluations across three model families on toxicity mitigation, sentiment redirection and sycophancy suppression show that LocUS matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines while intervening on under 6% of parameters and better preserving general capability.
summaryZh: LocUS 是一种针对大模型推理时激活干预的优化方法。传统方法通常在整个层表示空间进行干预，容易导致副作用。LocUS 通过识别嵌入矩阵中的特定属性线性子空间，并将干预限制在稀疏的注意力头中，实现了更精准的控制。实验表明，该方法在毒性缓解、情感重定向等任务上表现优异，且仅需干预不到6%的参数，有效保护了模型的通用能力。

模型将隐藏层状态映射回输出词表概率分布的矩阵。
